meaning:
μακροθυμέω, -ῶ
(μακρό-θυμος, long-tempered; see: -ία), [in LXX: Ecc.8:12 א2, Pro.19:11 (אָרַךְ, אַף אָרַךְ), Job.7:16, Sir.2:4, al. ;]
1. actively = καρτερέω, to persevere (Plut., 2, 593 F).
2. Passively, to be patient, long-suffering: absol., 1Co.13:4, Heb.6:15, Jas.5:8; before ἕως, with genitive, Jas.5:7; ἐπί, with dative, ib. (Sir.2:4); πρός, with accusative, 1Th.5:14; ἐπί, with dative, Mat.18:26, 29, Luk.18:7; εἰς, 2Pe.3:9.†
SYN.: ὑπομένω, q.v (AS)

elsewhere.note: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’
Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
We exhort you, brothers: Admonish the disorderly; encourage the faint-hearted; support the weak; be patient toward all.
Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it…
The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come…
